Is it good enough?

As the insurance SETTLED says it is: yes. The bar on record is "better than scale repair" — which fired 42 times in 30 days and left nothing — not "better than the direct render". The pipeline now works end to end in the Lab, refuses correctly when the declared depth is not real, keeps its evidence when it refuses, records its outcome in production, and the blend no longer destroys what the paste got right. The gate fires rarely by design, and the one systematic false trigger (shared vessels) is fixed at its source.
As a proven feature: not yet — three gaps, all cheap to close.
  • Blend v2 is one clean run on one page. The two regression pages the plan names (job_1786567053374 p4, job_1786571353564 p10 — good pages under the old prompt) have not been re-run. ~$0.12 settles whether v2 regresses them.
  • The objects[] gap is the last real build item. A prop-bearing depth page still loses its required objects — the plate prompt promises them with no source. Until then, composited pages are only safe when the props live in the empty-scene prose.
  • No production page has ever gone through end to end. Every fix is Lab-proven; the next gate-true story page is the real test, and since 14bcc6330 + c083dd396 it will document itself either way.

Open decisions for the owner: the push-gate blind spot (#29 — a cancelled-but-executing experiment reads idle, changing it changes what blocks prod pushes), and whether the no-avatar-no-VB walk-on should keep falling through to the direct render.
